scope: Make DRW_MPolygon DWG encoding transactional across caller body, string, and handle buffers, and verify allocation-failure rollback plus same-object retry together with the HATCH transaction regression.

changes: Run MPOLYGON validation, fill-color preparation, common data, body, detached strings, entity handle and boundary handles through encodeEntityDwgTransaction.
Keep the existing MPOLYGON wire order and fill-color profile checks; stage oType mutation and all caller streams until successful completion.
implementation.failureBehavior: Injected allocation failure leaves caller buffer bytes and bit positions, plus oType, unchanged; retrying the same entity against the same buffers reproduces clean successful encoding.

validation.allocationSweep: PASS: 1096 allocation offsets across HATCH and MPOLYGON, 6 DWG versions and 60 entity/version/stream-layout profiles

coverage: DWG writer versions AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032.
Five stream alias layouts per version: distinct streams, shared string/handle stream, body/string alias, body/handle alias, and all streams aliased.
A patterned associative MPOLYGON with a line boundary, boundary handle, fill color, x-direction vector, and degenerate-loop count is exercised.
Every observed injected allocation failure checks full stream rollback and object type restoration, then exact clean-output equality after same-object retry.
limitations: Generated allocation and retry controls establish transaction behavior only; they do not qualify physical DWG producer profiles, HATCH/MPOLYGON semantic fidelity, or native consumer acceptance.
No DWG or DXF drawing fixture was added.
